claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr contains approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
High configurational entropy in WTaTiVZr creates a nanoscale chemically disordered microstructure.
The chemically disordered microstructure stabilizes a fine grain structure.
Nanoscale chemical disorder and fine grains enhance dislocation mobility on multiple slip systems.
Nanoscale chemical disorder and fine grains may increase grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
The proposed microstructural state delays crack initiation and crack propagation during high-temperature loading.
Arc melting followed by forging and annealing can produce a fine, uniformly dispersed grain structure in WTaTiVZr.
Conventionally powder-metallurgy-processed, well-annealed pure tungsten has a coarse-grained state relative to the proposed HEA state.
Matching macroscopic dimensions and approximately matching grain size would isolate effects attributed to chemical disorder and lattice distortion.
A temperature near 1200°C is relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service.
High-entropy alloying in WTaTiVZr creates significant lattice distortions and a complex energy landscape.
The lattice distortions and complex energy landscape impede dislocation pile-up on any single slip system.
The lattice distortions and complex energy landscape promote activation of multiple slip systems.
Activation of multiple slip systems and reduced dislocation pile-up help arrest crack propagation.
Under equivalent high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under equivalent high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness and energy absorption before fracture than pure tungsten.
Processing differences or grain-size variations may dominate the measured mechanical response.
Refining tungsten's grain structure to approach that of WTaTiVZr may alter the observed performance difference.

contradictions.description: The initial-state specification assigns the HEA a fine grain structure and pure tungsten a coarse grain structure, while the controlled comparison proposes calibrating the two materials to similar grain sizes. These are incompatible comparison states unless separate matched-grain specimens are explicitly prepared.

The intervention proposes approximately grain-size-matched materials to isolate chemical disorder and lattice distortion, but the falsification design only controls sample dimensions and uses commercially processed tungsten; it does not explicitly require matched grain size or processing history.
